I read the whole file. It declares one theorem, `MonoidAlgebra.isPrimitiveElem_iff_eq_zero`, and no simp lemmas or attributes of its own, so the simp interface comes entirely from Mathlib lemmas. I checked those lemmas:
- `MonoidAlgebra.comul_single` and `MonoidAlgebra.counit_single` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/MonoidAlgebra.lean carry `(attr := simp)`.
- `tensorEquiv_single_tmul_single` in Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/MonoidAlgebra.lean carries `(attr := simp)`, and `tensorEquiv` has `simps! apply_coeff`.

The calls the proof makes are `simp only [...]` with explicit lemma lists and `simp [one_def, hg]` calls that rely on this coverage. I found no missing canonical simp lemma, no wrong rewrite direction, no competing rules and no plausible loop. The `simp only [...]; simp [...]; exact fun hg ↦ hg.symm` sequence in `hdiag` is a non-terminal simp that depends on the exact normal form. That is a proof-style matter, not a defect in the simp interface, and I could not run Lean to check how robust it is. The near-duplicate `hleft` and `hright` are also not simp-interface problems.
